_meta.purpose: Proves the Issue-13 value- and shape-level canonicalization rules in eval/compare.py: column matching by position (not name), NULL-sentinel normalization, float tolerance, and multiset (duplicate) semantics by default. Each case pins the exact 'rules' it exercises so the triple proves which canonicalization is responsible for the verdict — both the relaxations that must let an equally-correct query pass AND the boundaries that must still catch a real semantic error.
_meta.format: Each case: {id, description, gold_sql, gold_result:{columns,rows}, candidate_result:{columns,rows}, expected_verdict, rules:[...]} where expected_verdict is 'correct' | 'incorrect'. 'rules' overrides eval.compare.DEFAULT_RULES so each rule is proven in isolation. Loaded automatically by tests/test_compare.py.
_meta.scope: Row ordering is Issue 12 and is NOT exercised here. BIRD reconciliation and whole-fixture sign-off are Issue 14.

cases.description: Same values under renamed column labels → correct. Columns are matched by position, not name (CLAUDE.md domain rule 1); an alias/rename of a correct query must not fail it.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT name AS customer, total FROM orders ORDER BY name;

cases.description: Values swapped between column positions → incorrect. Position-based matching ignores labels but must still catch a genuine column-order error; it does not blindly pass everything.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT name, amount FROM orders WHERE id = 1;

cases.description: Both sides return a NULL in the same position → correct. NULLs normalize to one sentinel and compare consistently.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT phone FROM users WHERE id = 5;

cases.description: Gold NULL vs candidate 0 → incorrect. The sentinel is distinct from any real value, so a NULL never silently equals 0 (or '' or the string 'None').
cases.gold_sql: SELECT balance FROM accounts WHERE id = 9;

cases.description: Floats differing below the rounding tolerance (here in the 9th decimal) → correct. Insignificant precision noise from an AVG must not register as a wrong answer.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT avg(amount) AS avg_amount FROM payments;

cases.description: Floats differing above the rounding tolerance → incorrect. A genuinely different number must still be caught even with float tolerance applied.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT avg(amount) AS avg_amount FROM payments;

cases.description: Gold keeps duplicate rows (COUNT-style), candidate collapsed them (COUNT DISTINCT-style) → incorrect. Multiset is the default by omission of a de-dup rule, so a row-multiplicity difference is a real error. Under set semantics this pair would wrongly pass.
Both sides carry the same duplicate multiplicities → correct. Multiset semantics keep duplicates rather than collapsing them, so equal multiplicities compare equal.
